title: Mizuho Financial Group Uses Netskope to Scale AI Agent Development Securely
summary: Mizuho Financial Group, Inc., one of Japan’s leading global financial groups, is advancing AI Transformation to create new value for customers and society by augmenting employee capabilities and transforming business processes. At the heart of this initiative is the group’s in-house development lab. As Mizuho Financial Group accelerated the development of AI agents at scale, it faced a critical challenge: balancing security with developer productivity. To address this, the group deployed Netskope in its in-house development environment, establishing a security foundation designed to address emerging risks in the age of AI agents. With ongoing operational support from Netskope, Mizuho Financial Group is building internal expertise and know-how while exploring opportunities to extend its use of Netskope to other environments across the organization.
body_markdown:
The Digital Strategy Department plays a central role in driving AI Transformation across Mizuho Financial Group. Tatsuto Fujii, General Manager of the Digital Strategy Department and Chief AI Officer, explains how the organization has evolved. “The Digital Strategy Department was established in April 2025 through the reorganization of the former Digital Planning Department,” Fujii says. “We started with around 20 employees and have since grown to an organization of approximately 400 people, including partner companies. With AI at the center of our strategy, we are responsible for planning and managing DX initiatives across Mizuho. We work across organizational boundaries in collaboration with business divisions to advance AI Transformation, while demonstrating the benefits and costs of AI to senior management and building consensus around our initiatives.”


Fujii believes the AI agent era requires a new approach to security. “Because AI agents make decisions and take actions autonomously, guardrails are essential to control their behavior,” he explains. “We also need to be able to trace what data an agent used and how it reached a particular decision, as well as manage multi-agent environments. As AI agents increasingly connect with both internal and external systems, Mizuho Financial Group has defined its own design principles for AI agent development through AIOA, or AI Oriented Architecture. We will continue to evolve AIOA as AI technology advances.”


In accordance with Mizuho’s security standards and AIOA, the group has established three closely integrated components to drive AI Transformation: Mizuho Wiz Base, an AWS-based AI agent development platform; Agent Factory, a framework of shared capabilities for efficiently developing, evaluating, and improving AI agents; and the in-house development lab within the Digital Strategy Department. As AI agent development accelerated, however, the team encountered a key challenge: how to maintain strong security without compromising developer productivity.
